_about: What each entity's bodies are made of: the friction and restitution of its .ent, which the original hands the fixture it
builds (planning step 152, WT). DECODED, not guessed - and BOTH HELD, not applied, because the engine's solver does not do what
Box2D does with either (friction_applied and restitution_applied below say what, measured). What the port's bodies are built with
is the table's held_friction, the Godot project's 0 restitution, and the .ent's density as mass; the .ent's own friction and
restitution are kept here, read back by test_mp_timebase against the original's files, for the engine step that makes them true.
ETHPhysicsSimulator::CreateBody (reference/ethanon/toolkit/Source/src/
engine/Physics/ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:102-109) sets fixtureDef.friction = entity->GetFriction(idx) and
fixtureDef.restitution = entity->GetRestitution(idx) from the <Entity friction=... restitution=...> attributes of the .ent
(ETHEntityProperties.cpp reads them), and sets nothing else a material is made of: no damping (b2BodyDef's linearDamping and
angularDamping are Box2D's 0), so the port's bodies are built with none either (LevelBuilder::MakeRigid).
The solver mixes two surfaces as Box2D does and the engine's PhysicsSystem does: friction by the square root of the product
(CombineFriction), restitution by the larger (CombineRestitution). The port's player has friction 0 of its own (Player::kFriction:
its velocity is set every tick, and a gripping capsule fights its own walk), so a floor's friction touches only the loose bodies:
a crate, a stone, a barrel, a minion. A group whose DECODED friction is 0 (a minion, a gravity agent) applies it even while the
rest is held (apply_decoded_friction): 0 against any surface is 0, so no friction impulse is solved and the engine's solve is
not in the loop.
Every number below was read off the .ent in reference/extracted/assets/entities (the attribute named in each group's _source),
and the _no_emissive and _low_emissive variants of an entity carry the same pair, each checked. An entity this table does not
hold is built with the Godot project's constants (LevelBuilder::kBodyFriction 1, kBodyRestitution 0): these are the entity names
of the 128 levels that have no .ent among the extracted assets - moving_platform, moving_platform_single, enemy_killer, lava, bounce,
no_restitution, collision_128_sqr, single_block, double_block, square_platform_22, rocket_bridge, motor_seesaw - so their pair is
not decoded and stays the old guess (listed in the step's LEFT FOR LATER).
DENSITY is Box2D's mass: b2Body::ResetMassData sums density x area over a body's fixtures, and the group's `density` is the .ent's own
(a static's is 0, and `fixtureDef.density = entity->IsStatic() ? 0 : density`, ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:104). The port's mass is that
density times the AREA of the collider it builds - a box's, a circle's, a hull's, in metres - or `area_m2` where the port's collider is
simpler than the original's: a minion, a knight and the player are two circles of radius 1.3 x 14/2 = 9.1 units (0.182 m, the
compound `body {... radius = 1.3}` of ETHCompoundShape.cpp:69 over the 14 x 36 box), 2 x pi x 0.182^2 = 0.208139 m^2, and the port
builds one circle for a minion and a capsule for the player. So the player weighs 0.104, a barrel 0.432, a crate 0.538, a stone 1.131:
a barrel is 4.15 times the player, where every body weighed 1 before (planning step 152; it is what keeps 2-24's idle player on the
barrel, whose edge he stands on).
An entity with no density here, or that the table does not hold, keeps the engine's mass of 1.
_friction_applied: WHETHER A BODY IS BUILT WITH ITS ENTITY'S FRICTION. Today it is not: every friction below is DECODED and read back from its .ent
(test_mp_timebase), but a body and a surface are built with held_friction (below), as the port's were until planning step 152's
first build, and the .ent's own friction waits for an engine step. WHY, MEASURED. The engine's friction solve walks a RESTING box
sideways at a combined friction of about 0.4 to 0.6, and the decoded pairs of the game are in it: a crate on a platform is
sqrt(0.96 x 0.2) = 0.438, a barrel on a platform sqrt(0.7 x 0.2) = 0.374, on a block00 sqrt(0.7 x 0.4) = 0.529. Nothing of the
port is in the loop on the rig (test_mp_timebase, TheEngineWalksARestingBoxSidewaysAtTheDecodedFriction): a flat 30 x 30 crate, mass 0.144
or 1, set 1 unit over a flat floor, falls, lies level (rotation 0.000 deg, no spin, the contact normal exactly vertical) and then
accelerates along the floor to 5.745 units a second in 30 ticks and keeps it for ever, awake; a 29 x 38 barrel 8.78. The same rig at
1.0 against 1.0 sleeps after 30 ticks. On level 2-08 (level7a) a scan of the combined friction, every body at one value, over an idle
420 ticks: 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 slide a few units and stop, 0.44 and 0.5 creep at the end of the run, 0.6 and above hold. In the 128
levels (test_mp_pictures --sweep --bodies, tick 420, no input) 13 loose bodies, every one asleep at rest on the build before, were awake
at a constant 5.65 to 6.21 (nine crates) or 8.78 (four barrels) units a second with the decoded frictions: 2-05, 2-08 (two), 2-14,
2-15 (two), 2-17, 2-28, 2-32, 3-12, 3-15, 3-19, 3-30; 2-08's crate 854 reached button_827 and opened door_lift_823 on tick 264 with
nobody there. With every friction held there are none.
CAUSE, AS A HYPOTHESIS (the engine is not this step's to change). PhysicsSystem's velocity solve (PhysicsSystem.cpp, the loop
from `Velocity solve`, friction from about line 2058) derives the friction tangent AGAIN on every pass from the contact's current
relative velocity, and clamps the accumulated tangent impulse as one number against mu x the accumulated normal impulse as if along a
fixed axis, so after an overshoot the reversed direction has nothing left to give. The port's boxes have a depth in z, so a face on a
face is FOUR points, two to a corner, solved one after another (the engine's manifold count and order were NOT inspected). A Python MODEL
of that loop (out/parity/program/WT/fix1/solver_sim.py: four points, two at the left corner and then two at the right, 8 passes, gravity
40 m/s^2, no position correction) walks a 30 x 30 box at 5.55 units a second at 0.438 against the engine's 5.745, holds it at 0.3 and 1.0,
and walks it 0.00 at every friction when the tangent is held fixed per contact (Box2D's cross(normal, 1), the signed accumulation); but it
depends on that assumed point order (left, right, left, right gives 0.15) and at 0.6 it predicts 1.6 where the engine holds. A hypothesis
consistent with the measured band, not a diagnosis: the engine step that settles it is the owner's. TURN friction_applied ON WHEN
test_mp_timebase's tripwire fails (a resting crate at the decoded pair no longer creeps), then rerun every suite and the routes.
_held_friction: The Godot project's friction, 1 for a RigidBody2D and a StaticBody2D alike (LevelBuilder::kBodyFriction, kStaticFriction), which the
port's bodies had before planning step 152 and wave 3a's 86 routes were flown on. A body and a surface at 1 against 1 are 1: nothing
slides, nothing creeps (the rig above sleeps after 30 ticks). Not a decoded number: a held one, with the decoded numbers beside it.
_restitution_applied: WHETHER A BODY IS BUILT WITH ITS ENTITY'S RESTITUTION. Today it is not: every restitution below is DECODED and read back from its .ent
(test_mp_timebase), but the bodies are built with the Godot project's 0 (LevelBuilder::kBodyRestitution), and friction alone is applied.
WHY: the engine's solver applies restitution to a SPECULATIVE contact - a pair that is apart but closing within one step's travel
(PhysicsSystem.cpp:1574-1631: targetVelocity = max(-restitution x approach, -allowedApproach) for a pair with a gap) - so a body
with a restitution turns round BEFORE it touches, where Box2D turns it round AT the touch (a manifold has points only when the shapes
meet). MEASURED (test_mp_timebase, TheEngineBouncesAStoneBeforeItTouches): a stone of 0.15 dropped 100 units onto a floor turns round
5.00 units over it, falling at 567 px/s; the same stone with no restitution never turns round. With the decoded values applied,
test_mp_demolish's stone broke no wall (3 checks: it turned round short of the breakable it was thrown at) and one of test_mp_pictures'
walks changed; and any code of the port that asks whether two bodies TOUCH reads that gap. The engine is not this step's to change, so the flag
stays false and the bounce is a row of its own (LEFT FOR LATER: an engine step that applies restitution at the contact). Turn it on
there, and the suites that read a touch say what else has to follow.

groups._source: crate.ent, crate_no_emissive.ent, crate_small.ent, crate_small_no_emissive.ent: <Entity friction="0.960000" density="0.400000" restitution="0.200000">
crate_low_emissive.ent: <Entity friction="0.960000" density="0.400000" restitution="0.200000"> - the same pair as the crate group above; the group is its own only for the held_friction below
_held_friction: A GUESS (_guess true), not a decoded number: the friction this entity is BUILT with while friction_applied is false, in place of the
table's held_friction 1. crate_low_emissive is the crate of 3-13's slot (level12b; also level2b, level4b and level8c, where it is a
plain crate). WHY: the level is won by pushing this crate off its platform's edge into a 64 px slot between the platform (x 160) and
block00_1528 (x 96), where it must lie flat as a bridge (a 58 px crate in 64 px, a 2 px clearance under wall04): the player's walk is set
outright every tick, so a crate pushed along its platform moves at v = walk - mu x G / s, with mu the combined friction against the held
1 of the platform (sqrt(this x 1)), G 0.2954 u/tick^2 and s the player's share of the pair's mass 0.162 (R3b round 3, arithmetic checked
against traces): 0.58 u/tick at the held 1 (34.7 u/s), the decoded sqrt(0.96 x 0.2) = 0.438 would give 1.6 (96 u/s, the pace the 3a build won
at, release window 153-160) but is in the engine's creep band, and the crate then wedges as a 45 degree diamond under wall04 (bottom 132, a
top corner at y 142) on every release tick of 4,242 replays (R3b round 4). MEASURED on this build (out/parity/program/R3b/fix1/grid3.py:
the route's walk, the release tick scanned 125-260 at each value, 'won' = the player on the far side at the platform's level): the wedge
lets go, and the held walk pushes the crate down flat into the slot, for EVERY release from tick 180 to 259 at a value of 0.079 to 0.082 (a
combined 0.281 to 0.286), and only on isolated ticks at any other value tried except 0 (0.01-0.075: 0 to 7 of 55 or of 135; 0.083-0.4: 0 to
11; 0.0: 47 of 75, a crate that slides for ever, not taken). 0.08 is the plateau's middle. So the value is a knife-edge in the friction, and
the window in the INPUT holds for a continuous push and for a pause from tick 180 on (once the crate's centre is over the edge); a pause
in the push before tick 180 wedges the crate again but on isolated ticks (the restart button recovers it). The cost of a combined 0.283
against the decoded 0.438: the push is 1.89 u/tick (113 u/s) where the decoded pair would give 1.6, and a released crate slides a little
further; a resting crate does not creep (test_mp_timebase, NoLooseBodyOfAnyLevelCreepsAtRest: 108 asleep in the 128 levels, the 106 of
before and 3-12's two). To be dropped when the engine's friction solve is fixed and friction_applied goes true: the decoded 0.96 then
applies to this entity as to every other, and 3-13 is re-flown (at the decoded combined 0.436 the route's walk reaches the far side on at
most 1 release tick of 75).
